source.version: Published journal article, Batı Anadolu Eğitim Bilimleri Dergisi / Western Anatolia Journal of Educational Sciences, 2026, 17(1), 70-93; publication date 28 April 2026; DOI 10.51460/baebd.1757062 (PDF p. 1, printed p. 70). No different saved version is identified in retrieval.json.
source.title_on_document: ChatGPT Destekli Dönütlerin İlkokul Öğrencilerinin Yaratıcı Yazma Becerilerine Etkisi

supplement.where: Appendices Ek 1, Ek 2 and Ek 3, PDF pp. 22-24 (printed pp. 91-93). No separate external supplement is identified.
supplement.holds: Illustrative images of student texts during the intervention (Ek 1), student texts labeled as post-test examples (Ek 2), and ChatGPT example texts (Ek 3), PDF pp. 22-24 (printed pp. 91-93). No additional statistical tables, standard errors or confidence intervals appear there; the creativity results are in main-text Tables 6-8. The word banks visible in Ek 2 conflict with the post-test word bank in Table 3 (see task.description and reconciliation).

paper_design_summary: Two intact third-grade classes at one public school in Van were assigned by a class-name lottery to ChatGPT-supported instruction or control writing practice (PDF p. 8, printed p. 77, Çalışma grubu). For six weeks, the experimental class received AI example stories, teacher/peer feedback and guided rewriting, while the control wrote and shared texts without the additional feedback or instruction (PDF pp. 9 and 11-13, printed pp. 78 and 80-82). The researcher scored individual pre-test and week-8 post-test stories, with 30 analyzed pupils reported per arm; the post-test followed the intervention, but test-time AI availability, the relation of exclusions to analyzed counts, and the actual post-test word bank are not fully established (PDF pp. 10-12 and 15, printed pp. 79-81 and 84; PDF p. 23, printed p. 92, Ek 2).

studies.label: Class-randomized creative-writing instruction and subsequent story-writing test

assignment.what_was_assigned: Intact third-grade classes: the names of the school's eight third-grade classes were put into a bag; the first drawn class was assigned to the experimental condition and the next to control. There was one class per arm and no within-person assignment or crossover of AI conditions. Pre/post measurement is repeated, but treatment assignment is between classes; this is the meaning of assignment.structure here. The school was selected by convenience. The explicit lottery supports field_rct despite the author's quasi-experimental label.
assignment.quote: Okulda bulunan sekiz 3. Sınıf şubelerinin isimleri ayrı kâğıtlara yazılarak bir torbaya atılmış; ilk seçilen şube deney grubu, seçilen bir sonraki şube ise kontrol grubu olarak atanmıştır.
assignment.locator: PDF p. 8 (printed p. 77), Çalışma grubu, lottery paragraph; PDF p. 7 (printed p. 76), Araştırmanın modeli, author label; PDF p. 12 (printed p. 81), Table 4, repeated pre/post measurements in the same assigned groups.

arms.name: ChatGPT examples plus guided feedback and rewriting
arms.description: One class wrote an initial story, shared it and received peer feedback, examined a ChatGPT-generated story on the same theme with the teacher, and rewrote its own work. The teacher also explained creative-writing techniques. Students did not use ChatGPT individually (PDF p. 9, printed p. 78, ChatGPT; PDF p. 12, printed p. 81, intervention description). The reported analyzed count is from Tables 6-7, PDF p. 15 (printed p. 84).

arms.name: Writing practice without added feedback
arms.description: One class completed paper-and-pencil creative writing on the same weekly themes and shared texts with classmates, without teacher feedback or additional creative-writing instruction outside the usual lesson (PDF pp. 12-13, printed pp. 81-82, Table 4 and intervention description). The reported analyzed count is from Tables 6-7, PDF p. 15 (printed p. 84).

participants.exclusions: Before the creative-writing pre-test, basic-writing screening and teacher judgments led to exclusion of data from 4 experimental pupils and 5 control pupils with low writing skills (PDF pp. 10-11, printed pp. 79-80, Veri toplama süreci). The paper also describes 60 study participants (PDF p. 8, printed p. 77, Çalışma grubu and Table 1) and reports analyzed N=30 per arm in Tables 6-7 (PDF p. 15, printed p. 84). These explicitly printed analysis counts are retained. The paper does not reconcile the exclusions with them or give pupil counts at class assignment; n_randomized remains null. The analysis is not described as intention-to-treat.
participants.who: Third-grade pupils at one public school in Van; the extended abstract specifies the İpekyolu district and the 2024-2025 academic year. School selection was by convenience. Only pupil participants are counted; teachers, the researcher and a separate feasibility-pilot class are not added.
participants.quote: Araştırmanın çalışma grubu, Van ilinde devlet okullarının birinde 3. sınıfta öğrenimine devam eden 60 öğrenciden oluşmaktadır.
participants.locator: PDF p. 3 (printed p. 72), Extended Abstract, Method; PDF p. 8 (printed p. 77), Çalışma grubu and Table 1; exclusions and feasibility pilot: PDF p. 11 (printed p. 80), Veri toplama süreci; analysis counts: PDF p. 15 (printed p. 84), Tables 6-7.

ai_tool.name_model: ChatGPT, GPT-3.5, accessed through the OpenAI website, as reported (PDF p. 9, printed p. 78, ChatGPT).
ai_tool.how_used: The teacher entered the writing theme through an electronic classroom board to obtain an example narrative; the class read and compared that example with student-written texts, received teacher/peer feedback and rewrote its texts. The model did not directly receive each pupil's draft for personalized editing, and pupils did not individually chat with it. Thus the delivered AI content is coded as supplied examples, although the paper calls the instructional process feedback (PDF p. 9, printed p. 78; PDF p. 12, printed p. 81).

task.description: Individual narrative writing at pre-test and post-test, with imaginative, word-bank and collaborative story-writing exercises during the intervention. Table 3 gives the pre-test words as “Vatan, bayrak, asker, arkadaşlık, köy” and the post-test words as “Bütçe, aile, alışveriş, ihtiyaç, istek, yardım” (PDF p. 10, printed p. 79). However, the examples labeled “Son test haftası” in Ek 2 show the handwritten word list “Gökyüzü, uçurtma, şenlik, sabır, yağmur,” above the stories (PDF p. 23, printed p. 92). The source does not explain this mismatch, so the actual administered post-test word bank cannot be confirmed. Weekly practice texts and ChatGPT examples are illustrated in Ek 1 and Ek 3, but no separate weekly creativity scores are reported.
task.duration: Six intervention weeks, one day per week with three 40-minute lessons for the experimental class; eight weeks including preparation and the pre/post tests. The pre-test writing period was 40 minutes; a separate post-test duration is not stated (PDF p. 11, printed p. 80; PDF p. 12, printed p. 81, Table 4).

outcomes.name: Creative Writing Products Evaluation Scale total score on the post-intervention story
outcomes.measure_detail: The researcher scored student-written stories with Kasap's (2019) Yaratıcı Yazma Ürünlerini Değerlendirme Ölçeği, a unidimensional 24-item scale with each item scored 1-5 and a total range of 24-120; sample Cronbach alpha is .88 (PDF p. 8, printed p. 77, Veri toplama araçları; scoring by the researcher: PDF p. 11, printed p. 80). The researcher is the university-affiliated author (PDF p. 1, printed p. 70), so the measure is coded expert_raters; assessor blinding and inter-rater agreement are not reported. Performance bands are an alternative summary of this same score, not an additional outcome: low 24-48, medium 49-72, good 73-96, advanced 97-120 (PDF p. 9, printed p. 78, Table 2). PDF p. 15 (printed p. 84), prose between Tables 6 and 7, reports experimental pre-test counts of 26 low, 3 medium and 1 good, and control pre-test counts of 26 low and 4 medium; experimental post-test counts are 7 low, 6 medium, 12 good and 5 advanced, and control post-test counts are 25 low and 5 medium. Pre/post paired tests and the post-test eta statistics also summarize this same outcome. No separate novelty, fluency, flexibility, elaboration or between-person diversity scores are reported. No outcome is explicitly designated primary.
outcomes.delay: The scored post-test is a later session in week 8, after intervention weeks 2-7; the delay in days is not stated (PDF p. 11, printed p. 80, Veri toplama süreci, final paragraph; PDF p. 12, printed p. 81, Table 4). Table 4 lists ChatGPT feedback/support in the intervention row and story writing plus the evaluation scale in the post-test row, but does not establish whether AI assistance or prior AI examples were unavailable while the scored stories were written. Pupils' lack of individual ChatGPT use does not establish removal of teacher-mediated assistance (PDF p. 9, printed p. 78, ChatGPT). Accordingly ai_available_when_produced and question are null; neither with_ai nor after_ai can be confirmed. Timing remains delayed because the post-test occurred in a later session.

contrasts.treatment_arm: ChatGPT examples plus guided feedback and rewriting
contrasts.reported: Post-test, Table 6: Deney N=30, mean=73,40, S=24,61; Kontrol N=30, mean=40,23, S=11,33; sd=58, t=6.705, p=.000. Post-test, Table 8: η=.771, η²=.594. Baseline, Table 6: Deney N=30, mean=34,23, S=14,56; Kontrol N=30, mean=35,66, S=10,82; sd=58, t=-.433, p=.667. Additional within-arm comparisons of this same outcome, Table 7: experimental pre/post N=30 at each time, means 34,23 and 73,40, S=14,56 and 24,61, sd=29, t=-7.887, p=.000; control pre/post N=30 at each time, means 35,66 and 40,23, S=10,82 and 11,31, sd=29, t=-8.238, p=.000. Table 7 prints control post-test S=11,31, whereas Table 6 prints 11,33. The prose on PDF p. 16 instead labels both paired tests t(30). All values and p=.000 are retained as printed; no effect size, standard error or interval is computed. The eta/eta-squared entries are the paper's effect statistics, not standardized mean differences. No confidence interval or standard error is printed.
contrasts.locator: PDF p. 15 (printed p. 84), Tables 6 and 7; PDF p. 16 (printed p. 85), Table 8 and opening paragraph. Table 7 is titled Shapiro-Wilk results but contains the paired-comparison N, mean, S, sd, t and p columns; analysis methods identify paired and independent t-tests on PDF p. 13 (printed p. 82), Verilerin analizi.

eligibility.reason: All three core criteria are met. The explicit lottery assigned intact classes to teacher-mediated generative-AI examples and guided rewriting or no-AI writing practice: first draw experimental, next draw control (PDF p. 8, printed p. 77, Çalışma grubu; AI use and comparison procedures: PDF pp. 9 and 12-13, printed pp. 78 and 81-82). This supports field_rct despite the author's quasi-experimental label (PDF p. 7, printed p. 76). Tables 6-7 explicitly report 30 analyzed pupils per arm, meeting the people threshold; randomized pupil counts remain null because the paper does not reconcile the exclusions with these analyzed counts (PDF p. 15, printed p. 84; PDF p. 11, printed p. 80). The researcher scored pupils' written stories using the creative-writing product scale, satisfying the output criterion (PDF pp. 8 and 11, printed pp. 77 and 80). Test-time AI availability is unconfirmed, so ai_available_when_produced and question are null; this affects classification as with_ai or after_ai, not the established randomized AI intervention, analyzed sample, or scoring of human output (PDF pp. 11-12, printed pp. 80-81, post-test description and Table 4). Both conflicting post-test prompts describe creative stories and do not change the output criterion (PDF p. 10, printed p. 79, Table 3; PDF p. 23, printed p. 92, Ek 2). Only one class was assigned per arm and the reported pupil-level t-tests lack a class adjustment, limiting suitability of the reported precision for pooling without changing core eligibility (PDF pp. 8, 13 and 15, printed pp. 77, 82 and 84).

one_line_finding: Among 60 analyzed pupils, post-test creative-writing means were 73,40 after ChatGPT examples plus guided feedback and rewriting versus 40,23 after writing practice alone, t(58)=6.705, p=.000 as printed (PDF p. 15, printed p. 84, Table 6); one class per arm and bundled feedback limit attribution.
open_questions: Which post-test word bank was actually administered? Table 3 lists “Bütçe, aile, alışveriş, ihtiyaç, istek, yardım”, whereas the handwritten headings on the examples labeled as post-test texts in Ek 2 read “Gökyüzü, uçurtma, şenlik, sabır, yağmur,”. The document does not identify which is correct or explain the mismatch (PDF p. 10, printed p. 79, Table 3; PDF p. 23, printed p. 92, Ek 2).

How do the exclusions of 4 experimental and 5 control pupils relate to the explicitly reported analyzed N=30 per arm? Initial pupil counts at class assignment are not stated, and no alternative total is inferred (PDF p. 11, printed p. 80, Veri toplama süreci; PDF p. 15, printed p. 84, Tables 6-7).

Was ChatGPT, a previous AI example, or teacher-mediated AI assistance available while pupils produced their week-8 post-test stories? The protocol places the test after the intervention but does not establish removal of assistance, so ai_available_when_produced and question are null. Exact days since the final AI lesson and a separate post-test time limit are also not stated (PDF pp. 9 and 11-12, printed pp. 78 and 80-81, ChatGPT, Veri toplama süreci and Table 4).

The control post-test S is 11,33 in Table 6 but 11,31 in Table 7; paired-test df is 29 in Table 7 but t(30) in the next-page prose. Table 7 is also captioned Shapiro-Wilk results despite its paired-comparison columns. The correct SD, degrees of freedom and caption cannot be settled from the document, so the conflicting printed versions are preserved (PDF pp. 15-16, printed pp. 84-85).

No class-adjusted standard error or interval is reported. The study assigns one class per arm but uses pupil-level t-tests; the reported precision is unsuitable for pooling as a class-randomized effect (PDF pp. 8, 13 and 15, printed pp. 77, 82 and 84).
notes: Reconciled on 2026-10-09. Both raw forms were present and parsed. The full markdown was read in consecutive chunks through the references and all appendices. Relevant PDF pages were independently extracted with PyMuPDF; result Tables 6-8 and appendices Ek 1-3 were also inspected as images rendered in memory. All numerical data retained in the form were checked against the PDF; no effect size or missing sample count was calculated. Locators give one-based PDF pages and printed journal pages. The five reconciliation entries cover one assignment-structure disagreement and four differences in recorded detail: test prompts, sample reliability, performance-band cutoffs and performance-band counts. Wording variants, additional cautionary wording already present elsewhere, and relocation of baseline/paired statistics from A.notes to B.outcomes were not counted as substantive differences. All baseline, post-test, paired-test and eta statistics agreed across the complete forms and have been retained together in reported. The unresolved reconciliation entry concerns the actual post-test prompt; source limitations shared by both screeners remain separately in open_questions and do not inflate n_differences or n_unresolved. The sole scored creative-outcome construct is the total creativity score; performance bands and pre/post comparisons are alternative summaries of that same outcome. The basic-writing selection exercise and feasibility pilot supply no separate comparative AI-effect dataset, so they are not additional studies. The task-topic experts are not additional outcome raters. No weekly scored outcome, between-person diversity measure, preregistration, public data/code repository, sample reuse, or company involvement is stated. Assignment.structure refers to allocation of AI conditions; repeated baseline/post-test measurement does not make that allocation mixed. The author explicitly acknowledges that the intervention cannot separate ChatGPT from receiving feedback generally (PDF p. 16, printed p. 85, Discussion). Finalized on 2026-10-09 after an independent full read of the markdown, including references and appendices. Relevant PDF pages were extracted with PyMuPDF; Tables 6-8 and all three appendices were also inspected as images rendered in memory. All three challenge files were reviewed; the assignment and people files contained no problems, and the sole outcome problem was corrected. Test-time AI availability and the resulting question classification are null because the source does not confirm AI removal or availability during production of the scored post-test stories; none would incorrectly assert that the outcome answers none of the three questions. The reconciliation object is preserved unchanged as requested; its historical no/after_ai confirmation is superseded by the final correction. All reported numerical statistics are unchanged. The prompt issue in open_questions[0] and the unresolved reconciliation difference are addressed together in final.open_items. No remaining source question changes the three core criteria; the question category and pooling suitability remain separate limitations. Challenge counts count challenged problems, not unresolved source questions.

open_items.item: Actual post-test word bank (open_questions[0] and unresolved reconciliation.differences[1]): Table 3 and Ek 2 give different prompts. Author confirmation of the administered prompt and which examples belong to the scored test would settle it. Both descriptions involve student-written stories, so criterion 3 remains met (PDF p. 10, printed p. 79, Table 3; PDF p. 23, printed p. 92, Ek 2).

Participant flow (open_questions[1]): clarify how the four experimental and five control exclusions relate to the analyzed sample and supply pupil counts at class assignment. This would settle the missing randomized counts and flow, while the explicit analyzed N=30 per arm supports criterion 2 (PDF p. 11, printed p. 80, Veri toplama süreci; PDF p. 15, printed p. 84, Tables 6-7).

Test conditions and timing (open_questions[2] and the corrected outcome challenge): author confirmation of AI/example availability, teacher-mediated assistance, the interval since the last AI lesson, and the post-test time limit would settle the unconfirmed details. Availability determines with_ai versus after_ai; it does not change random assignment, the analyzed people count, or scoring of pupils' stories (PDF pp. 9 and 11-12, printed pp. 78 and 80-81, ChatGPT, Veri toplama süreci and Table 4).
